beats.trigger: ## Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new, a section title

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: The module is about files the agent keeps, not about chatting.

beats.trigger: (5) Optional: Lindenberg memory-architecture piece.
beats.got: Five reading items. I'll do the connectors and skip the rest.

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** whether memory is compounding or growing
beats.got: Build a memory, build an agent on it, and judge whether it improves. 'Evaluate' is the item I care about.

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: Asking gets an answer. Maintaining means the knowledge stays and gets updated. Fine, though the folder setup talk is fiddly.

beats.trigger: Connectors let the agent combine clues that live apart, like a wiki page and an email thread.
beats.got: My pricing pilot can be the challenge, and the agent can read across Confluence and email.

beats.trigger: The guardrail: propose or draft only, do not send, edit, book, or change anything.
beats.got: A scheduled agent that only drafts is safe enough to try. My CFO would ask about that rule first.

beats.trigger: Good: *The Q2 pricing redesign: usage-based vs. seats, pilot cohort, sales briefing.*
beats.got: The example is nearly my own project. I picked the usage-pricing pilot and the interview wrote the brief in a few minutes.

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: Narrow scope, a handful of topic pages, around 45 minutes.

beats.trigger: Always comply with your company's AI policy.
beats.got: Check data rules first. Nordveil's customer fleet data stays out, pricing docs only.

beats.trigger: Ask for a plan first.
beats.got: Ask for a plan before big reads. Sensible, nothing more.

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: The agent proposed sources and asked about my context. I pushed back on two of them.

beats.trigger: Aim for 8–10 items with real content or local-path links across lists (1) and (2); list (3) is usually empty.
beats.got: It pulled in about nine sources. The retrieval was slow, and some Confluence pages were unreachable.

beats.trigger: If two topics should merge or something is missing, give one sentence of feedback and ask for a revised plan.
beats.got: I read the topic split and merged two topics before it wrote anything.

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: The self-audit found that the churn article contradicts the Q2 review. That is the kind of finding I wanted.

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: A custom agent is a rules file, and citations show whether it used my files.

beats.trigger: Push back if a claim "got sharper" but the top didn't change.
beats.got: A new source rewrote existing claims instead of adding paragraphs. That is not a better prompt, it is better material.

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: It proposed cleanups, I rejected half, and it applied the rest. A short step.

beats.trigger: If the answer is specific and every claim has a citation, the memory works.
beats.got: I asked where the seats-vs-usage case breaks. The answer was specific and cited, and I'd use it with the working group.

beats.trigger: A system is *persistence* (files it reads again) plus *automation* (it runs).
beats.got: Files plus an agent that reads them. I already felt that.

beats.trigger: The second batch made the first batch better. That is compounding.
beats.got: nothing new, it repeats Phase 3

beats.trigger: A saved document with no agent is just a document. An agent with no files is a chat.
beats.got: nothing new, this is the third time persistence plus automation has been defined

beats.trigger: The existing memory was part of the prompt for updating the memory, so old and new claims met and the ones that couldn't survive got cut.
beats.got: The sharpening works because the agent reads the old pages first. That explains why my Phase 3 result got tighter.

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: Keep rules small and boring. Fine, but vague.

beats.trigger: No database, special tool or paid tier is needed.
beats.got: It's plain markdown, so it's portable. That also means my team could share one folder.

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: Three layers: sources stay untouched, memory gets edited, rules file governs. I'd use this separation for audit trails.

beats.trigger: *Generic AI becomes your AI when you build the memory it reads.*
beats.got: Answers carry my material instead of an industry take. A slogan, but true to what I saw.

beats.trigger: If a competitor could claim a page, the memory is growing but not compounding.
beats.got: A test for generic pages. The agent flagged three of mine that any pricing consultant could have written.

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.
beats.got: The agent only knows what is written. My team's pricing reasoning is mostly not written down.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the rules file from the session: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
beats.got: The agent drafts a root rules file from the session.

beats.trigger: What the agent leaves out is often the signal.
beats.got: Check what the summary skipped. It left out the contradiction I had to resolve by hand.

beats.trigger: Every miss is context the agent still lacks.
beats.got: A bad answer means missing context, so I fix the memory or the rule, not the wording. That moves me off the prompt-writing idea.

beats.trigger: The model will change under this. The memory will not.
beats.got: The folder is the asset and the model is replaceable. Useful for budget talks.

beats.trigger: Persistence plus automation: a system.
beats.got: nothing new, a recap

beats.trigger: Module 3 splits work against that week of runs; without it the split is guesswork.
beats.got: I need a week of scheduled runs before the next module.

take_homes: The memory I built on the pricing pilot is a folder of files. Updating it means feeding it sources and fixing its misses, not rewording prompts.
The self-audit and Phase 3 found contradictions and generic pages I hadn't seen myself.
A scheduled draft-only agent reading that folder gives me a daily risk scan, and I keep ownership of what leaves the system.

monday.move: Re-run the pilot-cohort brief from the pricing memory with fresh data, check the risk scan's first week, and send the brief to the pricing working group
monday.who: me, then the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: The scan flags only things I already know, or cites nothing outside my files, for three days running
monday.blocker: My fourteen people each keep their own copies of context files. There is no shared place for the folder, and this module only covered one person.

misconception.why: Phase 3 and the self-audit improved results by adding and editing sources, not by rewording a prompt. I still think prompt skill matters, but the memory carries more of it than I expected.

one_line: Good hands-on build on a real challenge, but the compounding part repeats itself and it never says how fourteen people share the folder.
